action: Fugaku users: revoke and replace SSH keys used with Fugaku, as RIKEN asks, and watch for phishing emails. Others: no action needed; for awareness.
date_note: Intrusion ran November 10-13 and Fugaku was shut down November 14; date is RIKEN's public notice of November 16.
exec: A national research supercomputer is offline with no restart date, and stolen credentials were used to connect to external systems.
impact: Fugaku has been shut down since November 14 and users' login keys were disabled.
plain: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer is still offline. RIKEN says data of 4,222 users and 430 login credentials were taken, and some credentials were used to connect to other systems.
summary: RIKEN's second notice (20 Nov) says 4,222 Fugaku users' data was taken, now including registration details, and 430 credentials (233 SSH private keys without a passphrase, 197 with one) were exfiltrated; for some, connections to external systems were confirmed. Fugaku stays offline with no restart date, and no attacker is named.
title: Japan's RIKEN takes Fugaku supercomputer offline after intrusion

validation.note: The Register, ITdaily and eSecurity Planet each report RIKEN's own statement; the RIKEN notice itself was not retrieved. The BleepingComputer page returned 404 on review and was removed. The Register adds that someone attempted to log in to Fugaku on November 13; eSecurity Planet says RIKEN confirmed attempts to use stolen credentials on other systems. The Register's text suggests the machine went offline on November 13; ITdaily and eSecurity Planet give November 14. RIKEN's own second notice of 20 Nov read; it gives 4,222 Fugaku users and does not mention the 375 Rikyu users or up to 4,597 total.

review.note: Compared title, 4,222 Fugaku users, 430 credentials (233/197 SSH keys), external connections for some, no restart date, no attacker against RIKEN 20 Nov notice; intrusion/shutdown dates rest on earlier press sources
